examples.en: The factory manager checks the machines every morning.

examples.ko: 우리 공장장은 직원들 이름을 다 알아요.
examples.en: Our factory manager knows the names of all the staff.

examples.ko: 새 공장장이 오고 나서 분위기가 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: After the new factory manager came, the mood changed.
Tell the factory manager about this problem first.

examples.ko: 아버지는 이 년 전부터 공장장으로 일하세요.
examples.en: My father has worked as a factory manager for two years.
The factory manager and the staff had lunch together.

explain: '-장'은 그곳을 책임지는 사람 이름에 붙어요. '팀장', '반장'처럼 써요. 부를 때는 '공장장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Hello, Factory Manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 부르거나 높여 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing or showing respect.

phrases.example: 그분은 십 년 일하고 공장장이 되었어요.
phrases.en: After working ten years, he became the factory manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 올랐다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone reaches that position.

phrases.en: Please talk to the factory manager about the schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 문제를 공장장과 의논할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when discussing work or a problem with the factory manager.
phrases.en_equiv: to talk with the factory manager

explain_en: '-장' marks the person in charge of a place or group, as in '팀장' and '반장'. When addressing the person you say '공장장님'.

en: to be reticent; to be reserved

examples.ko: 제 동생은 과묵해서 말을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: My sibling is quiet and doesn't talk much.

examples.ko: 과묵한 사람은 말은 적어도 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: A man of few words is trustworthy even if he says little.
My father is usually quiet.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 과묵하지만 경기에서는 늘 최선을 다해요.
examples.en: That player is reserved, but always does his best in games.

examples.ko: 과묵하게 앉아 있다가 갑자기 한마디 했어요.
examples.en: He sat silently and then suddenly said a word.
I become quiet in front of strangers.

explain: '말수가 적다'와 비슷하지만 '과묵하다'는 대체로 좋게 보는 말이에요. 조용하고 무게 있는 사람 같다는 느낌이 있어요. 반대는 '수다스럽다'나 '말이 많다'예요. 안 좋게 말할 때는 '무뚝뚝하다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: That teacher seems reserved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 받는 인상을 말할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아/어 보이다' for an impression from appearance.

phrases.en: I'm somewhat on the quiet side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편이다'를 쓰면 조금 부드럽게 성격을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '편이다' makes a description of personality softer.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on the reserved side

phrases.en: My father doesn't talk much.
phrases.nuance_ko: '과묵하다'와 비슷하지만 좋고 나쁜 평가 없이 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 과묵하다 but neutral, without praise or criticism.

explain_en: It is close to '말수가 적다', but '과묵하다' is generally a positive description, suggesting a calm, weighty person. The opposite is '수다스럽다' or '말이 많다'. For a less flattering tone, people sometimes use '무뚝뚝하다'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 그림을 너무 과찬하셔서 부끄러웠어요.
examples.en: My teacher praised my drawing so much that I was embarrassed.
My friend praised me too much, and my face turned red.
Please don't overpraise me. I still have a long way to go.

examples.ko: 칭찬은 고맙지만 너무 과찬하시는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Thank you for the compliment, but I think you're praising me too much.
I think people overpraised that movie.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람을 과찬하면 오히려 어색해요.
examples.en: Overpraising someone you've just met actually feels awkward.

explain: 칭찬받았을 때 겸손하게 '과찬이세요'라고 답하는 표현으로 많이 알려져 있어요. 동사로는 '너무 칭찬하다'라는 뜻이라서 내가 한 칭찬에는 잘 안 쓰고, 남이 한 칭찬을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: You say I draw well? You're too kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬을 받고 겸손하게 대답하는 말이에요. 윗사람에게 정중하게 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modest reply to a compliment, in a polite form suitable for someone older.
phrases.en_equiv: you're too kind (praising me too much)

phrases.en: I'm still lacking, so please don't praise me too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬이 지나치다고 부드럽게 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to say the praise is too much.

phrases.en: Saying my cooking is the best, you're praising me too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 한 칭찬을 동사로 받아서 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Responds to the other person's praise using the verb form.

explain_en: People often know it from the humble reply '과찬이세요' when complimented. As a verb it means praising too much, so you rarely use it for your own praise; you use it when talking about someone else's praise.

examples.en: In the army you learn training from an instructor.

examples.ko: 비행 교관은 저에게 먼저 안전 규칙을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The flight instructor first told me the safety rules.

examples.ko: 회사에서 안전 교육을 맡을 교관을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is looking for an instructor to run safety training.
Everyone ran in time with the instructor's commands.

examples.ko: 구조 훈련 때 교관과 함께 물에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: During rescue training I went into the water with the instructor.

examples.ko: 교관이 되려면 오랫동안 경험을 쌓아야 해요.
examples.en: To become an instructor, you need to build experience for a long time.

explain: 학교 선생님은 '교사', 학원 선생님은 '강사', 군대나 비행·구조처럼 기술을 훈련시키는 사람은 '교관'이라고 해요. 엄격한 훈련의 느낌이 있어서 일반 수업에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.example: 교관님이 훈련 방법을 자세히 설명해 주셨어요.
phrases.en: The instructor explained the training method in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교관을 높여서 부르거나 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '님' to address or refer to an instructor politely.

phrases.example: 비행 교관이 이륙 방법을 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: The flight instructor showed me how to take off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기 조종을 가르치는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who teaches how to fly an aircraft.

phrases.en: The training instructor was very strict.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 기관에서 훈련을 시키는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who runs training in the military or an institution.

explain_en: A school teacher is 교사 and a cram-school teacher is 강사. 교관 is for someone who trains people in a skill, such as in the military, flying, or rescue work. It has a strict-training feel, so it is not used for ordinary classes.

examples.en: The president visited France as a state guest.

examples.ko: 국빈 방문을 맞아 환영 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: A welcome ceremony was held for the state visit.
Many politicians attended the state banquet.

examples.ko: 이번 주에 일본 총리가 국빈 자격으로 오신대요.
examples.en: I hear the Japanese prime minister is coming this week as a state guest.
Because they are hosting a state guest, security is tight.
I was surprised to be treated like a state guest at the hotel.

explain: 나라가 정식으로 초청한 외국 손님을 가리키고 '국빈 방문', '국빈 만찬'으로 자주 나와요. '귀빈'은 중요한 손님 전체를 부르는 말이라서 범위가 더 넓어요.

phrases.example: 국빈 만찬에는 한국 전통 음식이 나왔어요.
phrases.en: Traditional Korean food was served at the state banquet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국빈을 위해 여는 공식 저녁 식사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official dinner held for a state guest.

phrases.en: They welcomed the foreign president with state-guest treatment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 아주 귀하게 대접한다는 뜻으로 비유적으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively to mean treating someone very specially.

phrases.example: 그는 국빈 자격으로 초대받아 연설을 했어요.
phrases.en: He was invited as a state guest and gave a speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 신분으로 참석하는지 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state in what capacity someone attends.

explain_en: Official guest of a state, such as a visiting head of state. It refers to a foreign guest formally invited by a country and often appears in '국빈 방문' and '국빈 만찬'. '귀빈' means an honored guest in general, so its range is wider.

examples.en: A distinguished guest is coming to today's event.
Those sitting in the VIP seats, please come this way.
The president attended as a guest of honor.

examples.ko: 호텔은 귀빈에게 가장 좋은 방을 줬어요.
examples.en: The hotel gave the best room to the VIP.
I was treated like a VIP, so I felt great.
Many distinguished guests gathered at the wedding.

explain: 공식 행사에서 높은 손님을 정중하게 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서 친구를 초대했을 때는 '귀빈'이 아니라 '손님'이라고 해요. 농담으로 '귀빈 대접을 받았다'고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Distinguished guests, please take your seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 행사에서 손님들에게 인사할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to address guests at formal events.

phrases.en: Today we hosted the president as a guest of honor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모시다'를 붙여 손님을 정중하게 맞이한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 모시다, it politely means to host a guest.

phrases.en: I was treated like a VIP at the hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별하고 정중한 대우를 받았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you received special, courteous treatment.

explain_en: Formal; honored guest at ceremonies and events. This is a polite word for an important guest at an official event. When you invite a friend in daily life, you say '손님', not '귀빈'. People also use '귀빈 대접을 받았다' jokingly.

examples.en: I have a friend who takes devoted care of his parents.

examples.ko: 엄마가 몸살을 앓는 동안 아버지는 엄마를 극진히 간호했어요.
examples.en: While Mom was sick with aches, Dad nursed her devotedly.
The owner welcomed us warmly and with great care.
The hotel staff look after guests with great attention.

examples.ko: 극진히 대접받아서 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was treated so lavishly that I didn't know how to react.

examples.ko: 선생님이 병든 저를 극진히 보살펴 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher took devoted care of me when I was ill.

explain: '모시다, 대접하다, 간호하다, 보살피다'처럼 사람을 정성껏 돌보는 말과 잘 어울려요. '정성껏'보다 더 깊고 예의 바른 느낌이라 어른이나 손님에게 하는 일에 써요. 형용사 '극진하다'의 부사형이에요.

phrases.en: The staff member attended to the guest with great devotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극진히'와 뜻이 같고, 형용사 '극진하다'에 '-게'를 붙인 형태라서 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 극진히; it is the adjective 극진하다 plus -게, and the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: My father treated his old friend with great hospitality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님에게 음식이나 마음을 정성껏 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving a guest food and heartfelt care.

phrases.en: I took devoted care of my grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아프거나 나이가 많은 사람을 정성껏 돌볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for caring for someone who is sick or elderly with great devotion.

explain_en: It goes well with verbs of caring for people, such as '모시다', '대접하다', '간호하다' and '보살피다'. It feels deeper and more courteous than '정성껏', so it suits things done for elders or guests. It is the adverb form of '극진하다'.

en: to be grave; to be austere

examples.ko: 교장 선생님은 늘 근엄한 표정으로 서 계세요.
examples.en: The principal always stands with a stern expression.
My grandfather looks stern, but he is warm inside.
The king sat solemnly and looked at his subjects.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 평소에 너무 근엄해서 말 걸기 어려워요.
examples.en: That teacher is so stern usually that it is hard to talk to him.
My great-grandfather in the photo looks very stern.
My once-stern father smiles in front of his grandchild.

explain: 엄숙하고 무게가 있어서 가까이 가기 어려운 태도에 써요. 주로 어른이나 지위 높은 사람의 표정, 목소리, 태도를 말할 때 많이 써요. '엄숙하다'는 분위기나 장소에도 쓸 수 있지만 '근엄하다'는 사람에게 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My father began speaking with a stern look on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근엄하다'를 뒤의 명사에 붙여 쓴 모양으로, 사람의 얼굴이나 태도를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adjective modifying a noun, often used to describe a person's face or manner.

phrases.en: The teacher spoke gravely, so the classroom became quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 동사를 꾸며서 말투나 행동을 설명할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -게 lets the word modify a verb to describe how someone speaks or acts.

phrases.example: 그분은 처음에는 근엄해 보였지만 알고 보니 친절했어요.
phrases.en: He looked austere at first, but he turned out to be kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 느껴진다는 뜻으로, 첫인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes how someone appears, so it is useful for first impressions.

explain_en: It describes a solemn, weighty manner that makes someone hard to approach. It is mostly used for the expression, voice or attitude of an elder or a person of high rank. '엄숙하다' can also describe an atmosphere or place, but '근엄하다' is used more for people.

examples.en: The president came to the meeting with his secretary in tow.
You can enter only if accompanied by a guardian.
The mayor visited the site accompanied by staff.

examples.ko: 어린이는 부모님을 대동한 경우에만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Children can enter only when accompanied by their parents.

examples.ko: 손님을 대동하실 때는 미리 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If you are bringing a guest along, please let us know in advance.

examples.ko: 가족을 대동하면 할인을 받을 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can I get a discount if I bring my family along?

explain: '데리고 가다'를 격식 있게 한 말로, 사람에게만 쓰고 물건에는 쓰지 않아요. 안내문이나 공문에서 '보호자 대동'처럼 자주 나와요. '동반하다'와 비슷하지만, '대동하다'는 누군가를 데리고 함께 간다는 쪽이에요.

phrases.en: I took a friend along to the gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대동하다'를 일상 말투로 쉽게 바꾼 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday, plain way to say 대동하다.

phrases.en: Children, please come with a guardian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request often seen in notices.

phrases.example: 보호자를 대동하지 않으면 들어갈 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You cannot enter without bringing a guardian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 가는 사람이 없을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when no one accompanies you.

explain_en: Formal; to bring people along, usually subordinates or juniors accompanying someone of higher status. It is a formal version of '데리고 가다' and is used only for people, never for objects. It appears often in notices and official texts, as in '보호자 대동'. It is similar to '동반하다', but '대동하다' leans toward taking someone along with you.

examples.en: I meet my family face to face after a long time.
The two people met face to face in the meeting room for the first time.
I was scared to face the other person in the accident.
I want to talk in person, not online.
I will meet the boss in person tomorrow.
You need the courage to face a hard reality.

explain: '만나다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '대면하다'는 직접 얼굴을 마주 본다는 점을 강조해요. '비대면'의 반대말로 뉴스와 회사에서 자주 들려요. '~을/를 대면하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I will meet the customer face to face tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '직접'을 붙이면 얼굴을 마주 본다는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 직접 makes the face-to-face meaning clearer.

phrases.en: We are holding the meeting in person this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 만나서 하는 회의를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A meeting held in person.

phrases.en: The class switched to remote (online) format.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대면'의 반대말로 만나지 않고 하는 방식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 대면, meaning without meeting in person.

explain_en: '만나다' works anywhere, but '대면하다' stresses meeting face to face in person. You hear it a lot in news and at work as the opposite of '비대면' (non-face-to-face). It takes an object: '~을/를 대면하다'.

dis.h: meet face to face, often confronting
gh: meet; everyday, any person or place

p.n: 만나다 is grammatical but loses the sense of facing the person directly (confrontation).

t90.ax: I want to talk in person, not online.

examples.ko: 학생들이 길 양쪽에 도열해서 손님을 맞았어요.
examples.en: Students lined up on both sides of the road to welcome the guests.
The president walked past the soldiers standing in formation.
The players are lined up at the entrance of the stadium.
The staff lined up at the entrance and waited for the boss.
Fans were lined up at the airport exit.
The graduates lined up side by side on the field.

explain: 행사에서 환영하거나 맞이하려고 사람들이 질서 있게 늘어서는 모습에 써요. 차례를 기다리며 서는 '줄을 서다'와는 달라요. 글이나 뉴스 느낌이 나서 일상 대화에서는 '나란히 서다'로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 아이들이 문 앞에 나란히 서서 선생님을 기다렸어요.
phrases.en: The children stood in a row in front of the door and waited for the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도열하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 'line up' and more natural in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The police officers are lined up along the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄 서 있는 상태가 계속되는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the continuing state of standing in line.

phrases.en: The players came in between the people lined up on both sides.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 꼴로 사람들을 꾸미는 표현이라 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing people, often seen in news reports.

explain_en: It describes people standing in an orderly row to welcome someone at an event. It differs from '줄을 서다', which is waiting your turn. It sounds like writing or news, so in daily talk people also say '나란히 서다'.

examples.en: Sir, though it's late, congratulations on the birth of your son.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 득남 소식을 전해 와서 온 가족이 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: My uncle sent word that he had a son, and the whole family was delighted.
I got word that my friend and his wife had a baby boy.
To celebrate the birth of his son, he handed out rice cakes to the staff.

examples.ko: 결혼 5년 만에 득남을 해서 집안이 기뻐해요.
examples.en: They had a son after five years of marriage, and the family is overjoyed.
What would be a good gift for a newborn son?

explain: 집안에서 아들을 얻었을 때 쓰는 축하의 말이에요. 딸이면 '득녀'라고 하고, 보통 '득남을 축하해요'처럼 다른 사람에게 말해요. 요즘은 성별과 상관없이 '출산'이나 '아기가 태어나다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My friend had a baby boy last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '득남'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형으로, 아들을 얻었다는 소식을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '득남', used when sharing news that someone had a son.

phrases.en: I heard the news of my senior's baby boy after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소식'과 함께 써서 남에게 들은 기쁜 소식을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '소식' (news) to talk about the happy news you heard about someone.

phrases.en: My older sister gave birth to a son yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '득남'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이라 누구에게나 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Simpler and more everyday than '득남', and fine to use with anyone.
phrases.en_equiv: to give birth to a son

explain_en: It is a congratulatory word used when a family gains a son. For a daughter, '득녀' is used, and it is usually said to someone else, as in '득남을 축하해요'. These days people also say '출산' or '아기가 태어나다' regardless of gender.

examples.en: Grandpa, happy birthday. I wish you a long and healthy life!
My parents' long and healthy life is my greatest wish.
I wrote 'long and healthy life' on Grandma's birthday card.

examples.ko: 손자들이 할아버지의 만수무강을 기원하는 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: The grandchildren sang a song wishing Grandpa a long and healthy life.
We all sincerely wish our teacher a long and healthy life.
I offered a wish for their long life and left the house.

explain: 어른의 건강과 장수를 비는 인사말이라 생신이나 회갑 같은 자리에서 써요. 윗사람께 '만수무강하세요'라고 하지만, 평소에는 '건강하세요'가 더 자연스러워요. 친구에게 쓰면 어색해요.

phrases.en: Grandma, I wish you a long and healthy life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른께 건강과 장수를 비는 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting wishing an elder good health and long life.

phrases.en: I pray for my parents' long and healthy life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '을/를 빌다'와 함께 쓰면 소원을 말하는 문장이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 을/를 빌다, it becomes a sentence expressing a wish.

phrases.en: Grandpa, please stay healthy for many years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소 윗사람에게 말할 때 더 자연스러운 쉬운 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more natural greeting to an elder in daily life.

explain_en: It is a greeting that wishes an elder good health and a long life, used at birthdays and 60th-birthday celebrations. You can say '만수무강하세요' to someone older, but in daily life '건강하세요' sounds more natural. It feels odd to say it to a friend.

examples.ko: 혼자 사시는 할머니께 말벗이 되어 드렸어요.
examples.en: I kept the grandmother who lives alone company by talking with her.

examples.ko: 퇴근 후에 말벗이 필요해서 친구에게 전화했어요.
examples.en: I needed someone to talk to after work, so I called a friend.
My dog is my only companion to talk to.
I signed up for volunteering to chat with elderly people.

examples.ko: 좋은 말벗을 만나서 시간이 빨리 갔어요.
examples.en: I met a good conversation partner, so the time flew by.

examples.ko: 말벗도 없이 먼 길을 혼자 운전했어요.
examples.en: I drove a long way alone without anyone to talk to.

explain: '말동무'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 외로운 사람 곁에서 이야기를 나눠 주는 사람을 말하고, '말벗이 되다/되어 주다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother is happy to have someone to chat with.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말벗'과 거의 같은 뜻으로, 바꿔 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '말벗', and the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: I live alone, so I have no one to talk to and feel lonely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기할 사람이 없어서 외롭다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you feel lonely because you have no one to talk to.
phrases.en_equiv: to have no one to talk to

phrases.en: My puppy is a good companion for me to talk to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곁에서 이야기를 들어 주는 고마운 존재를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a grateful presence who listens and keeps you company.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '말동무'. It refers to someone who keeps a lonely person company by chatting, and is often used as '말벗이 되다/되어 주다'.

en: to welcome; to receive; to take in

examples.en: My parents welcomed their son-in-law warmly.

examples.ko: 손님을 문 앞에서 맞아들여 거실로 안내했어요.
examples.en: I received the guests at the door and guided them to the living room.

examples.ko: 새 식구를 맞아들일 준비를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are getting ready to welcome a new family member.
The company welcomed the new team leader warmly.
If you welcome guests warmly, the atmosphere improves.

examples.ko: 며느리를 맞아들이는 날 집안이 잔치 분위기였어요.
examples.en: On the day they welcomed their daughter-in-law, the house felt like a feast.

explain: '맞이하다'는 새해나 계절처럼 넓게 쓰지만, '맞아들이다'는 사람을 안으로 들여 받아들이는 상황에 써요. 손님, 사위, 며느리, 새 식구처럼 집이나 조직 안으로 들어오는 사람에게 잘 맞아요.

phrases.en: This year our family welcomed a new daughter-in-law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 가족을 집안으로 받아들일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for welcoming a new family member into the household.

phrases.en: I cleaned the house to welcome our guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞아들이다'보다 쓰임이 넓어서 새해나 계절에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 맞아들이다; also used for the new year or seasons.

phrases.en: I opened the door and welcomed the guest inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님을 안으로 들여 맞이할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for letting a guest in and welcoming them.

explain_en: Welcome a guest inside — warm, written (손님을 맞아들이다) '맞이하다' is broad, as in welcoming a new year or season, but '맞아들이다' is for receiving a person and bringing them inside. It suits people entering a home or group, such as guests, a son-in-law, a daughter-in-law or new family members.

t90.ax: My parents welcomed their son-in-law warmly.
